title: Reference Call Prep One-Pager (Internal) — TEMPLATE
body:
Purpose
Use this one-pager to prep Redwood + the customer reference for a single reference call. This is internal-only and should be completed for every request (even if it’s “just 20 minutes”).

Owner + SLA
- Owner (who drives this doc to completion): [AE name] / [CSM name]
- CS approval required before scheduling?  Yes / No (default: Yes)
- Target SLA: first proposed times to prospect within 2 business days after reference confirms availability

-----------------------------
1) Request Snapshot (copy/paste friendly)

Prospect
- Company: [Prospect company]
- Segment: Startup / Mid-market / Enterprise
- Region/timezone: [e.g., US-Pacific]
- Stage: Discovery / POC / Security review / Procurement / Expansion
- Primary use case: [short description]
- Target deployment: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Deal owner: [AE]
- Supporting SE: [SE]
- CSM (if existing customer / expansion): [CSM]

Reference (customer who will take the call)
- Customer name: [Customer]
- Reference type approved: Reference call only / Case study + calls / Anonymized only
- Customer spokesperson(s): [Name, title]
- Backup spokesperson: [Name, title]
- Their deployment: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Use case alignment notes: [why this is a good match]

Scheduling
- Requested call length: 20 / 30 / 45 minutes
- Format: Zoom / Google Meet / Phone
- Proposed windows from reference customer: [3–5 options]
- Prospect constraints (hard deadlines, exec attendance): [notes]

Goal of this call (1 sentence)
- [Example: “Confirm Redwood can meet predictable p95 latency for a fintech auth flow on dedicated capacity and that the operational tooling is mature.”]

-----------------------------
2) What the Prospect Cares About (be specific)

Top 3 buying criteria (ranked)
1) [e.g., p95 latency under 900ms at steady-state, predictable under bursts]
2) [e.g., data isolation + controls, audit logs, KMS ownership]
3) [e.g., cost/token reduction vs current stack, batching/caching without breaking UX]

Known objections / risks
- [Security: SOC 2 / audit logs / retention / data residency]
- [Reliability: incidents, fallback behavior, throttling, rate limits]
- [Performance: long context, streaming stability, throughput, concurrency]
- [Commercial: minimum commit, dedicated capacity sizing, marketplace procurement]

Competitors / alternatives in play
- [List: build in-house, cloud managed endpoints, other inference vendors, incumbent LLM API]

Important nuance (what not to assume)
- Workload shape: [interactive vs batch; average input/output tokens; streaming or not]
- Region: [where users are]
- Sensitivity: [PHI/PCI/source code]

-----------------------------
3) Reference Customer Guardrails (must confirm before call)

Approval / boundaries
- Customer has agreed to participate in reference calls: Yes / No
- NDA required between prospect and customer?  Yes / No / Unknown
- Topics the reference customer will NOT discuss (verbatim):
  - [e.g., vendor pricing/discounting]
  - [e.g., internal security architecture]
  - [e.g., exact GPU types / capacity]
  - [e.g., exact token volumes]

Allowed to share (explicit)
- Deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private): Yes / No
- High-level architecture diagram verbally: Yes / No
- Quantified outcomes (ranges OK): Yes / No
- Reliability/incident learnings (non-sensitive): Yes / No

If anything above is “Unknown,” pause and get CS + Legal guidance before the invite goes out.

-----------------------------
4) Redwood Recommended Talking Points (choose 3–5)

Pick the themes that match the prospect’s evaluation criteria. Keep it concrete.

Performance + predictable latency
- Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput; how sizing was done
- Continuous batching / KV cache behavior (high level, no sensitive configs)
- Streaming stability and time-to-first-token patterns

Cost + production economics
- Batching + caching levers and how Redwood Console helped find wins
- Model/quantization recommendations (if customer used Redwood Optimize)
- How the team measured “cost per request” and avoided misleading comparisons

Reliability + graceful degradation
- Fallback policies (model variant/region) and how they’re configured
- What their on-call experience looks like (alerts, dashboards, runbooks)

Security + deployment flexibility
- Private deployment / VPC controls: customer-managed networking, audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations
- What security review looked like (evidence, timelines, who got involved)

Operations + rollouts
- Model version pinning, canary/A-B, rollback/fallback plans
- How they validated changes (prompt sets, evals, regression checks)


Optional: “What we wish we knew earlier” prompt
- Ask the reference customer to share 1–2 practical lessons learned (integration, measurement, rollout).

-----------------------------
5) DO / DON’T (share with everyone attending)

DO
- Do set expectations up front: “This is a peer-to-peer conversation; no pricing; please avoid confidential details.”
- Do encourage ranges and relative comparisons (e.g., “~30–40% reduction”) rather than exact volumes.
- Do keep examples tied to a defined measurement window (e.g., “over the first 30 days after cutover”).
- Do pause if the conversation drifts into sensitive areas and offer to follow up via Redwood.

DON’T
- Don’t discuss specific commercial terms, discounts, or contract language.
- Don’t share infrastructure specifics that could be sensitive: exact GPU counts, vendor SKUs, internal network topology.
- Don’t claim “guaranteed” performance beyond Redwood SLAs or beyond the reference’s specific workload.
- Don’t share other customers’ names, issues, or incident details.

Standard deflection line (use verbatim)
- “I want to be respectful of confidentiality—happy to talk about the approach at a high level, but I can’t share internal numbers or exact configuration details.”

-----------------------------
6) Agenda (recommended) + Moderator Script

Agenda (30 minutes)
- 0–3 min: Intros + boundary setting
- 3–8 min: Prospect context (prospect asks 1–2 questions about use case)
- 8–20 min: Reference customer story (deployment choice, implementation, outcomes)
- 20–27 min: Prospect Q&A
- 27–30 min: Wrap + next steps (Redwood team)

Moderator (Redwood) opening script (copy/paste)
- “Thanks everyone. Quick framing: this is a peer conversation to share experience using Redwood in production. Let’s avoid pricing, contract terms, and any confidential/security-sensitive details. If we hit a topic that’s better handled offline, we’ll capture it and follow up.”

Moderator close script (copy/paste)
- “Thanks—this was helpful. We’ll follow up with any open technical items on our side. [Prospect], we’ll send a short recap and proposed next steps by [date]. [Reference], thank you again—we’ll keep future requests lightweight and aligned to what you’ve approved.”

-----------------------------
7) SE Attendance Plan (primary + backup)

Primary SE role (choose one)
- Silent support (default): join muted/camera off unless needed
- Active support: answer technical follow-ups at the end
- No SE: only if call is non-technical and customer prefers fewer attendees

Backup SE attendee guidance
- Backup SE: [Name]
- When to pull in backup SE (check boxes):
  - [ ] Prospect asks about Private/VPC specifics (KMS/audit logs/data retention)
  - [ ] Prospect asks about latency benchmarking methodology (p95 windows, traffic replay)
  - [ ] Prospect asks about routing/fallback policy design
  - [ ] Prospect asks about rate limiting / 429s / quotas in Hosted API
  - [ ] Prospect asks about structured output / tool calling implementation

SE “minimal-intervention” playbook
- Let the reference answer first.
- If you jump in, keep it general and grounded: “In general, teams do X; details depend on workload.”
- Avoid roadmap commitments. If asked, say: “We can follow up after the call with what’s available today vs what’s planned.”

-----------------------------
8) Prep Checklist (must be done 24h before)

Logistics
- [ ] Confirm reference participant(s) and title(s) match what’s approved
- [ ] Calendar invite includes boundary language (no pricing/confidential)
- [ ] Confirm conferencing link works and time zones are correct

Alignment
- [ ] Share this one-pager with internal attendees
- [ ] Send reference customer a 3-bullet “what to expect” note
- [ ] Provide reference customer with 2–3 suggested questions from the prospect (optional)

Content readiness
- [ ] Confirm the 3–5 talking points we want reinforced
- [ ] Confirm “do not discuss” topics (and what to say instead)

Escalations
- [ ] If prospect is in security review, confirm with Naomi Feldman (Security/claims) if any phrasing is risky
- [ ] If prospect requests written statements or publication, route to Legal (Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes)

-----------------------------
9) Post-Call Notes + Follow-ups (complete within 24h after)

Outcome
- Did the call happen as scheduled? Yes / No
- Sentiment: Positive / Neutral / Negative
- Biggest prospect takeaway (1–2 sentences):
  - [ ]

Open items
- Owner + due date:
  - [Item] — [Owner] — [Due]

Reference customer feedback
- How did it feel for them? (time burden, comfort level)
- Any new boundaries requested?

Reference health
- Mark reference readiness status: Green / Yellow / Red
- Next allowed request window (if they gave one): [date range]

HubSpot hygiene (don’t skip)
- Log as activity on the prospect + reference customer records
- Tag: “Reference Call” + include who attended and summary

-----------------------------
Appendix: Calendar Invite Footer (recommended)

“Reference call note: This is a peer conversation focused on implementation experience and operational learnings. Please avoid pricing/discounts, contract terms, and confidential/security-sensitive details. If any topic is better handled offline, we’ll capture it and follow up separately.”

Appendix: Quick question bank (if prospect needs prompting)
- “What did your baseline stack look like before Redwood, and what drove the change?”
- “How did you evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and what tipped the decision?”
- “How did you measure latency/cost changes (window, p95/p99, traffic shape)?”
- “What operational tooling mattered most (dashboards, alerts, rollouts, fallback)?”
- “What would you do differently if starting today?”
